jess_acme: Hey team, since we moved our calls to GCP PSC the calls to api.redwood.run from prod start failing ~10% with TLS handshake errors and some 502s. Happening only from the prod subnet.
sam_support: sorry to hear that. Can you paste the curl + error and any traceroute/tcpdump you have? Also, did you change egress / NAT after PSC cutover?
jess_acme: Yep. Quick repro from a prod VM:

curl -v https://api.redwood.run/v1/embeddings -H \"Authorization: Bearer ****\" -d '{"input":"test"}'
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.run/v1/embeddings
* Hostname in DNS cache was 10.100.5.12
*   Trying 10.100.5.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.run (10.100.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: SSL: certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) TLS handshake error

sam_support: ok, two quick possibilities: 1) your egress IP that reaches Redwood is not in the allowlist and their infra is rejecting or terminating, 2) SNI/Host header is being rewritten by a proxy (PSC + internal proxy chain can alter SNI). Can you try --resolve to bypass DNS and also test with --tlsv1.2 -v ?

jess_acme: did --resolve mapping to the PSC private IP and got same cert error but different text:

curl --resolve api.redwood.run:443:10.100.5.12 https://api.redwood.run/v1/embeddings -v
* Connected to api.redwood.run (10.100.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS SNI server name: internal-svc-abcdef
* TLS error: server certificate name mismatch

lucy_engineering: that SNI value is the internal PSC target hostname. Looks like your proxy (our internal edge) is rewriting SNI to the backend name instead of preserving client SNI. If SNI doesn't match api.redwood.run Redwood will present a cert for their public hostname and handshake will fail.

sam_support: also check your Cloud NAT / egress. PSC often uses private IPs to reach the service but the outbound may still go through NAT to the internet for certificate validation/OCSP checks. What is the effective egress IP of your subnets? You can check with:

curl -s https://ifconfig.co

jess_acme: prod NAT egress IP is 35.208.11.42 (Cloud NAT). We thought PSC traffic stays internal but our proxy does hairpin and then the reply goes via NAT.

sam_support: two actions:
1) Make sure your edge/proxy performs TLS passthrough (preserve client SNI and host) to the PSC endpoint so Redwood sees api.redwood.run as SNI.
2) Ask Redwood to allowlist your Cloud NAT egress 35.208.11.42 OR configure NAT so PSC traffic exits from an allowlisted IP. Until one of these is done their infra may drop or misroute the handshake.

jess_acme: how do we check if SNI is being rewritten by the proxy? We use an internal envoy terminator in front of PSC.

lucy_engineering: in Envoy check the listener filter chain. If you have TLS termination (tls_context) at the edge then it's terminating, and downstream connection will use upstream TLS with upstream SNI set via \"sni: \"%DOWNSTREAM_PEER%\"\" or value configured. Look for `sni` in the cluster config. If it's set to the internal target it's wrong. You want the upstream SNI to be the original hostname (api.redwood.run) or do passthrough.

jess_acme: found it. Upstream cluster had sni: \"%UPSTREAM_HOST%\" which resolves to the internal PSC target. Changing to sni: \"api.redwood.run\" for that cluster fixed the SNI. Also we opened a ticket with Redwood to add 35.208.11.42 to their egress allowlist as a short term measure.

sam_support: nice. Can you repro now?

jess_acme: after config change + NAT allowlist update we get 200s. Quick test result:

curl -v https://api.redwood.run/v1/embeddings -H \"Authorization: Bearer ****\" -d '{"input":"ok"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.run (10.100.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake complete, server certificate OK
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"data":[...]} 

sam_support: great. To summarize next steps: - leave SNI change in config (or enable strict TLS passthrough) - coordinate with Redwood to keep your NAT egress IP in their allowlist (or use a static egress IP range documented in infra) - if you want fully private flow consider using Redwood Private or Dedicated options

jess_acme: thanks all. Will monitor and follow up if anything flares.

deploy-bot: Deployment of envoy config to prod finished (revision 2026-03-17T15:12:41Z) :rocket:

sam_support: marking this as resolved for now, reopen if you see regressions :thumbsup:
